title: Protocol for assessing the healthspan of Caenorhabditis elegans after potential anti-aging drug treatment
protocol: Maintain wild-type worms in NGM plates seeded with E. coli OP50 until gravid adult at 20°C (2–3 days).
Wash the plates with sterile M9.
Pipette the M9 across the plate several times to loosen worms and eggs that are stuck in the bacteria.
Collect the liquid in a sterile 15 mL conical centrifuge tube with cap.
Let worms settle for approximately 5 minutes.
Remove most of the water carefully, so as not to disturb the loose worm pellet.
Make the lysis solution by mixing 0.3 ml 5 M NaOH with 1.2 ml bleach and 3.5 ml H2O.
Add the solution to the centrifuge tube with the worms.
Rock the tube gently back and forth for about 3–5 minutes.
Check periodically, as intact worms will start to dissolve over time.
When most worms have dissolved, shake or vortex the tube vigorously to dissolve any remaining corpses.
Spin the tube in a desktop centrifuge for 1 min at 1,300 × g to pellet released eggs.
Aspirate the supernatant and leave about 0.1 mL solution in the tube.
Add sterile M9 buffer to reach a total volume of 12 mL.
Shake or vortex well for a few seconds.
Repeat steps e and f as necessary.
Transfer the precipitate with 5–10 mL sterile M9 to a clean petri dish.
Place the plate in a constant temperature incubator at 20°C.
After about 16 hours, transfer synchronous nematodes to NGM plates seeded with E. coli OP50 until they reach L4 stage, which takes 48 hours at 20°C.
Streak fresh E. coli OP50 on a new LB agar plate and incubate the plate at 37°C for 16 hours.
Inoculate 5 mL of liquid LB with a single colony from the E. coli OP50 streak plate, shake at 180 rpm, 37°C for 16–24 hours.
Seed the fresh 35 mm NGM plates with 250 μL of the fresh E. coli OP50 liquid culture.
Add 2 μM Usnic acid to the autoclaved NGM media before pouring for drug treatment plates.
Allow the seeded plate to dry on a super clean workbench.
Transfer 30 synchronized L4 animals to each of the fresh 35 mm NGM plates at 20°C.
Transfer worms daily for the first 10–14 days and every second day thereafter.
Mark nematodes that do not respond to mild stimuli as dead.
Exclude animals that climb down from plates or show unnatural deaths from analysis.
Synchronize nematodes and treat for 10 days with or without drug (2 μM Usnic acid) starting at L4 larvae stage.
Transfer nematodes to fresh plates seeded with E. coli OP50 every two days to avoid starvation.
Prepare a 2% agarose solution by dissolving 2% agarose in water and heating it in a microwave.
Place 50 μL of the 2% agarose on a middle slide between two pieces of tape on separate slides.
Wait about one minute, then remove the top slide to leave the agarose pad attached to the bottom slide.
Mount worms onto an agarose pad for imaging.
Take images with Zeiss Imager M2 microscope at magnification 10 (objective) × 10 (eyepiece).
Use excitation wavelength of 400 nm and detection wavelength of 570 nm.
Synchronize nematodes for the experiment.
Treat synchronized L4 larvae stage nematodes with or without 2 μM Usnic acid for 10 days.
Measure lipofuscin fluorescence in treated worms versus control using a microscope with 10× objective and 10× eyepiece magnification.
Set excitation wavelength to 400 nm and detection wavelength to 570 nm.
Open the fluorescent image using Image J software.
Convert the image type to 8-bit.
Invert the image.
Calibrate the image by selecting Uncalibrated OD.
Adjust the threshold of the image.
Select measurements for mean gray value, limited to threshold settings.
Analyze intDen data.
Record and sort all intDen values using Excel.
Input sorted data into analysis software for significance analysis and mapping.
Synchronize nematodes at L4 larvae stage.
Treat nematodes with or without drug (2 μM Usnic acid).
Transfer nematodes to fresh plates seeded with E. coli OP50 to avoid starvation.
Measure body bend rate of 20 individuals from control and experimental plates on days 5 and 10 of life from L4 stage.
Place worms in 20 μL M9 buffer on a glass slide for measurement.
Film worms using a Zeiss Imager M2 microscope.
Synchronize nematodes for treatment.
Treat synchronized L4 larvae stage nematodes with or without 2 μM Usnic acid starting on day 0.
Measure body bend rate of control and treated nematodes on days 5 and 10 in liquid.
Count the number of body bends per minute from 60 seconds film for each worm.
